title: Someone new is moving unnaturally fast
lede: Three weeks in and it is intense: constant contact, enormous declarations, talk of moving in, gifts beyond the stage of the relationship, and mild irritation whenever you are unavailable. It feels wonderful and something in you is uneasy.

blocks.text: Three weeks in and it is intense: constant contact, enormous declarations, talk of moving in, gifts beyond the stage of the relationship, and mild irritation whenever you are unavailable. It feels wonderful and something in you is uneasy.

items: Intensity is not intimacy. Intimacy is built from accumulated small reliability; intensity can be manufactured in a fortnight by anyone willing to.
The pattern to watch is not the flattery — it is the reaction to a small, ordinary boundary. That single test carries most of the diagnostic weight.
Fast escalation serves a function: it invests you heavily before you have seen how they behave under mild frustration.
Early over-disclosure of trauma creates false closeness and makes later withdrawal feel like cruelty on your part. That effect is sometimes engineered and sometimes just sad.

items.move: Slow it down on purpose and observe
items.detail: Not a rejection — a test. "I want to take this a bit slower" is the cheapest diagnostic available and it costs you nothing with a good person.
Friends, gym, family, routine, your own place. The first casualty of this pattern is always your independent life, and it goes quietly.
Say no to a single evening. Watch the response carefully. Fine and warm, or wounded and punishing?

items.move: Refuse financial entanglement at this stage
items.detail: No joint accounts, no lending, no co-signing, no cards. Whatever the story, the timeline is the problem.

items.move: Talk to one friend honestly, including the uneasy part
items.detail: Say the doubt out loud. Isolation from candid friends is what allows these patterns to run.
Vague feelings get argued away. A dated note of the exact behaviour does not.

items.say: "I really like this. I want to go slower — I do things better when they build."
"I am seeing friends on Thursday and I am keeping that."
"I am not ready to promise that yet. Not because of you — that is just my timeline."
"You seem angry that I had one evening to myself. That worries me more than the evening does."

items: Interpreting jealousy as depth of feeling. It is a control signal, not a compliment.
Giving up your own home, job, or friendships inside the first months.
Explaining away a frightening reaction because the apology afterwards was enormous. The cycle is the pattern.
Keeping the doubts from everyone who knows you, so nobody can tell you what they see.
If they responded to the slow-down warmly, you have learned something genuinely good. Proceed.
If they punished it, believe the punishment rather than the apology. The apology is the part that is repeatable at will.
Keep one account, one document folder, and one friendship that are entirely yours, permanently. Good relationships are undamaged by this.
Re-read your dated notes at three months. It is the clearest picture you will get.

limit: If leaving feels frightening, if your phone or money is monitored, or if you have been cut off from friends and family, that is coercive control. Contact a domestic abuse helpline before you announce any decision — the period around leaving is statistically the most dangerous.
